summary: Wachirabenchathat Park, commonly called Rot Fai (Railway) Park, is a large public green space in Chatuchak. It suits an unhurried outdoor visit for cycling, walking, jogging, picnicking and family recreation, with adjacent Queen Sirikit and Chatuchak parks extending the walk.
whyGo: Cycle or walk beneath mature trees on routes in a spacious city park.
Combine a picnic or exercise with playgrounds, sports facilities and water activities listed by the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration.
Visit the Bangkok Butterfly and Insectarium within the park grounds, subject to its own operating hours.
bestFor: Families and active visitors looking for a free outdoor break
Cyclists who want a dedicated park outing
Travellers already visiting the Chatuchak area
skipIf: You want a short, tightly scheduled indoor attraction or guaranteed guided activities.
You need confirmed step-free routes, accessible toilets or equipment hire; these details were not found in the official listing.
You plan to visit at midday and are sensitive to Bangkok heat.
duration: Planning estimate: allow 1–2 hours for a relaxed walk or cycle; allow half a day if combining the neighbouring parks and other facilities.
cost: Park admission is free. Rentals, boat activities, sports facilities and food may cost extra; current prices were not listed in the BMA park page, so confirm on site.
hours: The BMA’s Greener Bangkok listing gives daily hours of 04:30–21:00 and lists cycling during the same hours. Separate facilities may keep different schedules.
bestTime: Go early morning or late afternoon for a cooler walk or ride. December is usually a more comfortable period for outdoor activity than Bangkok’s hotter months, but daily conditions vary.
gettingThere: The park is on Kamphaeng Phet 3 Road in Chatuchak. The BMA lists BTS Mo Chit and MRT Phahon Yothin, Chatuchak Park and Kamphaeng Phet stations, plus multiple buses on Phahonyothin and Kamphaeng Phet 2 roads. The park is large, so check the entrance location before choosing a station or bus stop.
booking: No booking is indicated for general park entry. The BMA lists cycling, boat activities and sports facilities, but does not publish current rental rates or reservation arrangements on the park page; check with the relevant facility if these are central to your visit.
accessibility: The official page lists park activities and toilets but does not describe step-free routes, accessible toilets, wheelchair hire or path surfaces. Contact the park at 02 537 9221 to ask about specific access needs. Distances inside this large park can be considerable.
practicalTips: Bring water, sun protection and comfortable shoes; shade varies across the grounds.
Use the official park listing or call ahead to confirm facility and rental availability before making a special trip.
Cycling is allowed in the listed 04:30–21:00 window; follow signs and share paths carefully with walkers.
The butterfly garden is in the park’s southeastern area; verify its separate opening status before planning around it.
decemberNotes: No December 2026 holiday hours, closures or special events were published in the sources reviewed. Check the BMA listing or call the park nearer the visit. Cooler-season outdoor weather is a general seasonal expectation, not a forecast.
uncertainties: The official listing confirms park hours and free admission, but does not state current bike or boat rental prices, stock or operating schedules.
Accessibility details and path conditions were not documented in the BMA source reviewed.
The butterfly garden and sports facilities may have separate hours or availability; confirm directly.
December 2026 event and holiday schedules were not yet confirmed.
